exposure: neonates born to mothers without COVID-19 diagnosis
neonates born to mothers with COVID-19 diagnosis
outcome: pregnancy-related complications (hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, fetal distress)
neonatal weight, length, and head circumference
cohort: 586 neonates born to mothers with COVID-19 and 1535 neonates born to mothers without COVID-19
finding: COVID-19 in pregnancy was associated with increased maternal and neonatal complications, and cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of newborn COVID-19 diagnosis, while breastfeeding and skin-to-skin contact were not.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was significantly associated with newborn COVID-19 diagnosis, suggesting vaginal delivery as the safest mode when possible.
birth_weight: Lower neonatal weight in infants born to mothers with COVID-19 diagnosis
